title: Deep learning reveals more than 500 previously unrecognized earthquakes beneath David Glacier
summary: A deep-learning analysis of regional Antarctic seismic records identified more than 500 previously unrecognized intermediate-depth earthquakes roughly 100–150 km beneath David Glacier in East Antarctica. The earthquakes occur within a tectonic plate rather than at a plate boundary. The authors explain the concentration through bending stresses associated with variable thermally driven uplift and an abrupt change in lithospheric strength; the ice sheet may also affect regional stress.
ai_technology: Deep-learning seismic-event detector applied to regional seismic records
organization: University of Alabama; Complutense University of Madrid; University of Oklahoma

evidence.tested: A deep-learning analysis of regional Antarctic seismic records identified more than 500 previously unrecognized intermediate-depth earthquakes roughly 100–150 km beneath David Glacier in East Antarctica.
evidence.unknown: The discovery concerns a newly recognized concentration of intraplate events, not a new earthquake mechanism conclusively proven. Proposed stress sources are interpretations; the paper notes similar events elsewhere may remain undetected.
evidence.ai_role: Detected intermediate-depth earthquake signals in regional seismic data that were not recognized in prior catalogs; the authors then located and interpreted the events using seismological and geodynamic analysis.
